SUMMARY OF ESSENTIAL ELEMENTS OF CITING/REFEREE’S REPORT/INCIDENT FOOTAGE
Lifted the player, through the horizontal and dropped him on his head.
ESSENTIAL ELEMENTS OF OTHER EVIDENCE (e.g. medical reports)
FR8 was uninjured and able to play on.
SUMMARY OF PLAYER’S EVIDENCE
Player (“Fiji 92”) reviewed the video footage and accepted the RC and acknowledged the offence. Fiji
92 also noted that he was attempting to catch the player and not drop him, but was unable to hold
him. Before leaving the field of play, he apologised to FR8 and shook hands.
FINDINGS OF FACT
Fiji 92 accepted the RC and therefore we move to sanction.
Reg. 17.18 - Seriousness of the Incident
The first stage is to consider the seriousness of the incident to determine the entry point for the sanction. The
factors I have considered from Reg.17.18 include:
(a) The tackle was reckless.
(b) The ball carrier was lifted above the horizontal plane and landed on his head.
(c) The incident was avoidable but Fiji 92 does attempt to pull out of the tackle and catch the player as he
falls. He tries to lower the player safely but was unable to do so.
(d) FR8 was not ‘driven’ into the ground but rather was dropped.
(e) FR8 was uninjured.
In all the circumstances noted above, I believe that a low-end entry point of 6 weeks is appropriate.
17.19 Mitigating Factors
The second stage is to consider mitigating factors under Reg. 17.19. Factors I have considered are:
(a) Fiji 92 acknowledged the offence and accepted the RC.
(b) Fiji 92 has never received an RC in his rugby career.
(c) Fiji 92’s conduct at the hearing was very polite and respectful.
(d) Fiji 92 approached FR8 immediately after the incident and apologised.
(e) FR8 was uninjured.
For these reasons, I award full mitigation to Fiji 92 of 50% and, therefore, the sanction will be reduced to 3
matches.
In making this decision, I have considered the terms of Reg.17.19.3 which allows the JO to apply sanctions lower
than 50% of the lower end entry sanction where:
251130 Disciplinary Decision Siqila (Fiji) DXB 7s Page 2 of 6

(a) There are off-field mitigating factors; and
(b) The sanction would be wholly disproportionate to the level and type of offending.
In this case, I believe that Fiji 92’s acknowledgment and apology satisfy the first leg; however, I do not consider
the sanction to be wholly disproportionate. I believe that Fiji 92 did attempt to prevent FR8 from landing on his
head but the fact remains that Fiji 92 has a responsibility to ensure that FR8 landed safely, which he was not
able to do. Therefore, I do not consider that I am able to lower this sanction below 50% as I do not consider the
sanction to be wholly disproportionate and the sanction remains at 3 matches.
17.20 Aggravating Factors
I am not aware of any aggravating factors in this situation.
Matches / tournaments included in the sanction
Total sanction is 3 matches. Matches included in this sanction are:
1. HSBC SVNS Cape Town – 06.12.25; Fiji’s first pool match.
2. HSBC SVNS Cape Town – 06.12.25; Fiji’s second pool match.
3. HSBC SVNS Cape Town – 06.12.25; Fiji’s third pool match.

SUMMARY OF ESSENTIAL ELEMENTS OF CITING/REFEREE’S REPORT/INCIDENT FOOTAGE
Direct contact to head with a high degree of danger; no mitigation
ESSENTIAL ELEMENTS OF OTHER EVIDENCE (e.g. medical reports)
Incident occurred in the last play of the game.
NZ15 subsequently passed an HIA.
SUMMARY OF PLAYER’S EVIDENCE
Player (“Fiji 6”) reviewed the video footage and accepted the RC and acknowledged the offence. Fiji
6 also noted that the tackle was made in the last play of the game with Fiji defending a narrow lead
and there was no malice in the tackle. Fiji Coach also added that Fiji 6 was attempting to wrap with
his left arm.
FINDINGS OF FACT
Fiji 6 accepted the RC and therefore we move to mitigation.
Reg. 17.18 - Seriousness of the Incident
The first stage is to consider the seriousness of the incident to determine the entry point for the sanction. As
this incident involved head contact, the first note to Appendix 1 of Reg.17 confirms that the entry point must be
at least mid-range. The factors I have considered from Reg.17.18 include:
(a) The tackle was reckless.
(b) The tackle involved shoulder to the head of the ball carrier.
(c) There was no provocation that I am aware of.
(d) The incident was avoidable.
(e) The offence was completed in a reckless manner but without premeditation;
(f) The incident occurred in the last play of the game with Fiji defending a narrow lead. NZ scored from
this play to win the match.
(g) Neither player was injured.
The first note to the World Rugby Sanctions states that:
“Any act of foul play where the person committing the act of foul play makes contact with an opponent’s head
and / or neck, and that contact with the head and / or neck warrants a red card, shall result in at least a mid-
range sanction.”
251130 Disciplinary Decision Vunaki (Fiji) DXB 7s Page 2 of 6

In all the circumstances noted above, I believe that a mid-range entry point of 6 weeks is appropriate.
17.19 Mitigating Factors
The second stage is to consider mitigating factors under Reg. 17.19. Factors I have considered are:
(a) Fiji 6 acknowledged the offence and accepted the RC.
(b) Fiji 6 has never received an RC in his rugby career and has been playing on the international circuit for
3 years without any previous RCs.
(c) Fiji 6’s conduct at the hearing was very polite and respectful.
(d) Fiji 6 was unable to shake hands with NZ15 as he was with the physio at the time but he did try to see
the player.
(e) NZ15 was uninjured and passed a HIA.
For these reasons, I award full mitigation to Fiji 6 of 50% and, therefore, the sanction will be reduced to 3
matches.
17.20 Aggravating Factors
I am not aware of any aggravating factors in this situation.
Matches / tournaments included in the sanction
Total sanction is 3 matches. Matches included in this sanction are:
1. HSBC SVNS DXB - 30.11.26; Fra v Fiji –3rd place play off.
2. HSBC SVNS Cape Town – 06.12.25; Fiji’s first pool match.

title: World Rugby FPRC Decision Sergio Manoel Silveira De Luna BRA
text:
FOUL PLAY REVIEW COMMITTEE
DECISION
PARTICULARS OF OFFENCE
Player’s surname Sergio Manoel Silveira Player’s De Luna
forename(s)
Player’s Union Brazil
Match Brazil v Namibia
Competition Men’s Rugby World Cup Aus 2027 Qualifier Match Date 18 November 2025
SELECT: Red card ☒ Citing ☐
Offence Law 9.13 - A player must not tackle an
opponent early, late or dangerously.
Dangerous tackling includes, but is not
limited to, tackling or attempting to tackle
an opponent above the line of the shoulders
even if the tackle starts below the line of the
shoulders
Finding of Committee Foul play determined.
Foul play determined? Red Card upheld.
Red card upheld?
Summary of Sanction Three (3) week suspension. Should the Player apply for and successfully complete the Coaching
Intervention Programme the suspension may be reduced to (2) weeks.
Matches/tournaments Translated under Reg 17.21.3 (e) to the following three (3) sevens tournaments
included in sanction
Match 1 22 -23 November 2025 - Campeonato Paulista
Match 2 29 -30 November 2025 - Campeonato Paulista / Lions
Match 3 6-7 December 2025 - BR Sevens
The Player will be free to play in Match 3 if he applies for and completes the Coaching
Intervention Programme.
REASONS FOR DECISION
Evidence
1. The FPRC received and considered the following material:
a. video clips of the incident;
b. two (2) Match Official Reports from the Referee and TMO;
c. medical report, reflecting that the victim player Namibia #9 was removed from play for displaying obvious on-
pitch signs of concussion (Criteria 1) under the HIA protocol.
d. the Player’s submissions.
Disciplinary Decision Foul Play Review Committee Page 1 of 2

Decision
2. The Red Card threshold was met. The FPRC upheld the Red Card applying the Head Contact Process (2023):
a. head contact – Yes. The Player’s head made direct contact with the Namibia #9’s face and/or head;
b. foul play – Yes. The Player’s actions were reckless. He was always upright;
c. degree of danger – High. There was direct head-on-head contact. The Player was dynamic. There was high
force as the Player approached at pace without slowing down; and
d. mitigation – None. The Player had clear line of sight. He did not make an attempt to change his height or
speed. He did not have control. There was no significant drop or movement from Namibia #9
Sanction
3. The FPRC applied the mandatory mid-range entry point of 6 weeks due to the head contact.
4. Based on the Player’s clean disciplinary record the FPRC applied full mitigation 3 weeks (reducing sanction to 3
weeks).
5. In accordance with Reg 17.21.3 (e) - each tournament or Series of Matches played over a weekend shall be
considered to equate to one week for the purposes of calculating the suspension of a Player arising from a fifteen-
a-side Match, which applies to the following tournaments on the Player’s schedule
• 22 -23 November 2025 - Campeonato Paulista
• 29 -30 November 2025 - Campeonato Paulista / Lions
• 6-7 December 2025 - BR Sevens
6. The player is eligible for the Coaching Intervention Programme. If the Player applies and completes the
programme, the suspension may be reduced to two (2) weeks.

SUMMARY OF ESSENTIAL ELEMENTS OF CITING/REFEREE’S REPORT/INCIDENT FOOTAGE
At the 52nd minute of the match, a Red Card was issued against the Player for a breach of Law 9.11
(reckless or dangerous action):
“Following a review from the TMO, it was established that the player intentionally kicked an opponent
in the face on the ground, which was deliberate and highly dangerous. I then issued the player with a
permanent red card.”
ESSENTIAL ELEMENTS OF OTHER EVIDENCE (e.g. medical reports)
From video clips:
The Player, having received the ball from his scrum half as the first runner off a ruck, moved the ball
on quickly to the man outside him (#10). The opponent (Brazil #16) had been preparing to make a
front on tackle on the Player and was in a good low body position to do so, but continued to make the
tackle even although the ball had left the hands of the Player.
The tackler’s initial contact on the Player was to the outside of his right leg, the Player then having
turned side on to the tackler as he had pivoted that way as he made his pass to #10. The Player was
brought to the ground as the tackler slid downwards on the Player’s legs, ending up around, and
holding, his ankles.
By then the ball had been passed on and the tackle was late.
The Player ended up with his front of body towards the ground, both hands on the ground and with
both feet on the ground, with the tackler’s hands initially still on or around the Player’s ankles.
The Committee observes that with both hands on the ground and with both feet on the ground, the
Player was in a position to stand up, by drawing his feet forward and pushing up from his hands, if his
legs had been free to be moved.
With his left foot on the ground, the Player with his right foot now freed and without looking behind
him, lifted the right foot some height off the ground and at the same time propelled that foot, with
the sole and studs leading, in the direction of the opponent, making contact with the left side of the
opponent’s neck.
The opponent is seen to clutch at that area of his neck; whilst the Player replaces his right foot on the
ground (the left foot had stayed on the ground) and stands up and resumes play.
The photographs of the opponent’s neck show some abrasions to the side of the neck, lower down
the neck towards the shoulder area, consistent with stud marks. No other injury appears to have been
sustained.
251116 Disciplinary Decision Berguet (Belgium) FQT Page 2 of 7

SUMMARY OF PLAYER’S EVIDENCE
The Player’s written explanation follows verbatim:
“1. I was tackled from behind and held by the Brazil player despite no longer being in possession of
the ball.
2.My sole intention was to return to play as quickly as possible, and my immediate reaction was to
free my legs from his grip.
3. I had no visibility of the opponent’s body position, and therefore no deliberate or reckless intention
to make contact with him.
4. Immediately after the match, I approached the opponent to apologise. His words, as well as the
handshake and the embrace we exchanged, made it very clear that he viewed the incident as part of
normal play and not as foul play (refer to video attached).
5. Since I started playing rugby, I have never received a red card.
For these reasons, I respectfully submit that my action does not meet the threshold for a red card, and
I humbly ask to be allowed to participate on Tuesday in what is the most important match of my rugby
career.”
He was examined by the Committee members on this account, particularly on his points 1-3 inclusive.
Under that examination he candidly told the Committee that he was ashamed that he had reacted in
the way that he had and that he had “reacted the wrong way” in trying to get himself released from
being held by his ankles as quickly as possible. He said that he had no intent to injure or hurt the
opponent but just wanted to be let go.
He told the Committee that there was no excuse for acting in the way that he did and that he should
not have done so.
FINDINGS OF FACT
The matters already set out in the sections above as to what can be seen in the video clips and the
Player’s evidence suffice to set out the Committee’s conclusions. The Committee did not accept the
Player’s contentions in his point 3 above – the kicking action by him was deliberately made and made
recklessly as to the potential consequences which could (and did) follow.
In the end, it matters not that the opponent’s tackle was late; frustrated reactions cannot be
countenanced or allowed; especially when a reaction is performed by a kick which makes contact onto
an unprotected neck. Fortunately, no serious injury resulted, which may speak to the extent of actual
force involved.
On the balance of probabilities, the Committee finds that this was an intentional kicking out by the
Player in the direction of where there was a known opponent, carrying with it the very real risk, if not
certainty as it turned out, that contact would be made with the opponent. In his own words his action
taken, in kicking up and back, “was to free my legs from his grip.” And that action constituted physical
abuse of an opponent.
The Player knew (and effectively acknowledged this in his evidence when being questioned by the
Committee) that there was a real risk of the sort of contact which did occur, but in his heated
(over)reaction took that risk anyway.
251116 Disciplinary Decision Berguet (Belgium) FQT Page 3 of 7

DECISION
DECISIONS:
1. The Player accepts that there was foul play but disputed that a Red Card was warranted.
2. By a combination of WR Reg. 17.15.3 and 17.16.1(b) the Player had the onus to show that the Referee
was wrong to issue a Red Card and that this Committee must not make a finding contrary to the Referee’s
decision unless the Committee was satisfied on the balance of probabilities that the Referee’s decision
was wrong.
3. The Player has not satisfied the onus upon him; on the contrary this Committee is adamantly of the view
that the Referee’s decision was the correct one and the only one that could have been made in these
circumstances.
4. However, the Referee, having concluded that the Player’s action was an intentional kick, should have
considered the Player’s foul play as being a breach of Law 9.12 (physical abuse by kicking) rather than a
breach of Law 9.11 (a reckless or dangerous action).
5. The Committee discussed this with the Player and determined that amending the alleged foul play
offence to one of physical abuse by kicking (Law 9.12) could be made by it without causing injustice
(pursuant to WR Reg. 17.26.2), prior notice having been given to the Player and submissions heard on his
behalf. An intentional kick was, and at all times remained, the fundamental factual allegation leading to
the Red Card. Nothing changed in that regard; the same basis remained. A charge more appropriate was
substituted.
6. On that amended charge the Committee upheld the Red Card – it was warranted for an intentional kick,
carried out with recklessness as to the nearness of his opponent, and that opponent’s head and neck, and
the possible consequences.

title: FPRC decision Santiago Lopes POR
text:
FOUL PLAY REVIEW COMMITTEE
DECISION
PARTICULARS OF OFFENCE
Player’s surname Lopes Player’s Santiago
forename(s)
Player’s Union Portugal
Match Portugal v Uruguay
Competition November Internationals 2025 Match Date 8 November 2025
SELECT: Red card ☒ Citing ☐
Offence Law 9.13 – A player must not tackle an
opponent … dangerously. Dangerous
tackling includes… tackling … an opponent
above the line of the shoulders.
Finding of Committee
In the 17th minute of the second half of the match, with Uruguay on attack, the Player infringed
Foul play determined? by tackling an opposing ball carrier in an upright and dangerous manner, resulting in direct
contact by his head with the opponent’s head, in the facial area. The Player was yellow carded
Red card/Citing upheld?
on the field by the Referee and that card was upgraded to a 20-minute Red Card by the TMO
(also acting as the FPRO).
The FPRC determined that there was foul play by the Player – a breach of Law 9.13 and that the
Red Card should be, and is, upheld.
The Player initially was in a semi-crouched position as he led into the tackle, but rose upwards
immediately before contact, thereby making contact directly to the face of the opponent with
some force.
Summary of Sanction
Starting point: such a tackle involving, as it did, head contact “shall result in at least a mid-range
sanction”. Mid- range sanction warranted on the facts here, but not any higher.
Mitigating features were found present, and no aggravating factors.
Discount allowed at 33% given the factors listed in Reasons below.
So, from a starting point of a suspension for 6 weeks/matches, a reduction to 4 weeks. The
Committee grants the Player permission to apply for WR’s Coaching Intervention Sanction
Mitigation (CISM), and should he successfully complete the CISM, a reduction of a further
week/match will be applied.
Matches/tournaments
All rugby (whether XVs or 7s, and including all internationals and club fixtures) from 8
included in sanction
November 2025 up to and including 30 November 2025, if successful completion of the CISM
(including internationals Portugal v Hong Kong, Portugal v Canada, RC Montemor v Cascais (1st
Round, Honra Top 12) and any club matches in that period); should he not successfully
complete the CISM, all matches up to and including 7 December 2025 (which would then
include Wolves v Lusitanos and any other club matches in that additional period).
251110 FPRC Disciplinary Decision - Santiago Lopes (Portugal) Page 1 of 2

REASONS FOR DECISION
1. The Player rising upwards when entering and initiating contact.
2. Contact direct to the opponent’s head.
3. No HIA required; although a cut to eyelid which was sutured later, without further
complications.
4. Immediate acceptance of responsibility; and apology made to opponent.
5. Not a clear disciplinary record. – 1 previous red card in 2024, but not relating to a dangerous
tackle.
6. Allowing a 33% discount – from a 6-week starting point down to a 4-match suspension from all
rugby, whether internationals or club, XVs or 7s.
7. The Player is eligible to apply to WR for the application of the CISM which, if successfully
completed, would reduce the suspension to 3 matches.

text:
FOUL PLAY REVIEW COMMITTEE
DECISION
PARTICULARS OF OFFENCE
Player’s surname Sapsford Player’s Ollie
forename(s)
Player’s Union Rugby Australia
Match Australia A v Japan XV
Competition - Match Date 18 October 2025
SELECT: Red card ☒ Citing ☐
Offence 9.11 Players must not do anything that is
reckless or dangerous to others including
leading with the elbow or forearm, or
jumping into, or over, a tackler.
Finding of Committee Foul Play admitted
Foul play determined? Foul play determined.
Red card upheld? Red Card upheld.
Summary of Sanction Three (3) week suspension. Should the Player apply for and successfully complete the Coaching
Intervention Programme (if applicable) the suspension may be reduced to (2) weeks.
Matches/tournaments Three (3) matches for :
included in sanction
Match 1 ACT Brumbies v HKCR - 8 November 2025
Match 2 ACT Brumbies v Western Force - 30 January 2026
Match 3 ACT Brumbies v Waratahs - 4 February 2026
The Player will be free to play in Match 3 if he applies for and completes the Coaching
Intervention Programme, if applicable.
REASONS FOR DECISION
Evidence
1. The FPRC received and considered the following material:
a. video clip of the incident;
b. five (5) Match Official Reports from the Referee, Assistant Referees, TMO and FPRO;
c. victim player’s (Japan 14) statement and medical report;
d. the Player’s submission. There Player accepted foul play but did not accept that the Red Card threshold was
met.
Disciplinary Decision Foul Play Review Committee Page 1 of 2

Decision
2. The FPRC upheld the Red Card applying the Head Contact Process (2023):
a. head contact – Yes. The Player’s right shoulder made contact with Japan #14’s neck and/or head;
b. foul play – Yes. The Player’s actions were reckless. He was upright and he admitted he got his positioning
wrong;
c. degree of danger – High. The Player was dynamic. There was high force (Japan #14 described “intense
contact”); and
d. mitigation – None. The Player had clear line of sight. He did not make an attempt to change his height. There
was no significant drop or movement from Japan #14.
Sanction
3. The FPRC applied the mandatory mid-range entry point of 6 weeks due to the head contact. There was no injury
and the victim player played on. There was no basis for moving to top end.
4. Based on the Player’s clean record and experience the FPRC applied full mitigation 3 weeks (reducing sanction to
3 weeks). The player is eligible for the Coaching Intervention Programme, if applicable. If the Player applies and
completes the programme, the suspension may be reduced to two (2) weeks.
Note:
In the FPRC’s view, the appliable foul play for this incident should be Law 9.13 – Dangerous Tackling instead of Law 9.11.
Whilst there are no provisions under the Expedited Off-Field Sanctioning process which would permit the FPRC to amend
the appliable foul play, the FPRC notes the mandatory mid-range entry point for both 9.11 and 9.13 is the same.

FOUL PLAY REVIEW COMMITTEE
DECISION
PARTICULARS OF OFFENCE

forename(s)

Match BIL v Australia
Competition BIL Tour 2025 Match Date 2 August 2025

Offence 9.20 Dangerous play in a ruck or maul.
(a)A player must not charge into a ruck or
maul
Finding of Committee Foul Play not admitted.
Foul play determined? Foul play determined.
Red card upheld? Citing upheld.
Summary of Sanction Four (4) week suspension reduced to (3) weeks upon successful complete of the coaching
intervention programme.
Matches/tournaments Four (4) matches for Leinster:
included in sanction
Match 1 13 September 2025, Leinster vs Cardiff [pre-season]
Match 2 26 September 2025, Leinster vs Stormers [URC]
Match 3 11 October 2025, Leinster vs Sharks [URC]
Match 4 18 October 2025, Leinster vs Munster [URC]
The Player will be free to play in Match 4 if he completes the coaching intervention programme
REASONS FOR DECISION
Evidence
1. The FPRC received and considered the following material:
a. Citing Commissioner’s Report;
b. victim player’s (AUS#10) statement;
c. Australia team doctor’s report that AUS#10 failed the HIA (i.e. suffered a concussion);
d. written submission on behalf of the Player;
e. testimonial from Chief Operating Officer of Leinster Rugby.
Disciplinary Decision Foul Play Review Committee Page 1 of 2

2. The Player did not accept that he committed an act of foul play1 and argued:
a. he made contact with the upper body and shoulder AUS#10, not AUS#10’s head;
b. he made an attempt to bind with both arms but there was no space for his right arm;
c. the contact which caused the head injury to AUS#10 was made by BIL#19’s knee, subsequent to the Player’s
contact with AUS#10.
Decision
3. The Red Card threshold was met. The FPRC upheld the Citing applying the Head Contact Process (2023):
a. head contact – Yes. The Player’s right upper arm and/or elbow made contact with the right side of AUS 10’s
head, which was consistent with video footage (01:27) and AUS#10’s statement on a heavy blow to the right
side of his head. Contact by BIL#19’s knee was to the top of AUS#10’s head (00:44);
b. foul play – Yes. The Player’s actions were reckless. AUS#10 had already set in position at the ruck prior to the
Player’s approach. The Player had time and clear line of sight. The Player did not bind with his right arm.2 He
approached at pace from distance; launched off his right foot and dropped his right shoulder with his upper
arm and/or elbow making contact with AUS#10’s head;
c. degree of danger – High. The Player approached from a distance, at speed and did not slow down. He was
dynamic;
d. mitigation – None. The Player had time and clear line of sight. The Player did not have control – he
accelerated from a distance; he did not slow down and he lost his feet. AUS#10 braced for contact but there
was no significant drop or movement.
Sanction
4. The FPRC applied the mandatory mid-range entry point of 6 weeks due to the head contact. There was no basis
for moving to top end.
5. As the Player denied foul play, the FPRC did not agree to full 50% mitigation. Based on the Player’s clean record
and experience the FPRC applied a reduction of 2 weeks (reducing sanction to 4 weeks).
6. The Player applied for and is eligible for the coaching intervention programme, which the FPRC approves.
Foul Play Review Mike Mika (NZ)
Committee Members
Valeriu Toma (ROM)

Chair
Wang Shao-Ing

At 78.46 game time, #11 Samoa charged into a ruck with a tucked right shoulder making direct contact with the head of USA
#4. The Player did not bind onto another player, had a clear line of sight, head contact was avoidable and the act was always
illegal (tucked arm, leading with the shoulder). This was an act of foul play. The degree of danger was high as there was
direct contact with force to the head of USA #4. The Player’s actions were always illegal and there is no mitigation.
HCP Step 1: Has Head Contact Occurred?
a. Yes. The Player’s head made contact with the USA #4’s face and/or head.
HCP Step 2: Was there foul play?
b. Yes. The Player charged into a ruck with a tucked right shoulder making direct contact with the head of USA #4. The Player
did not bind onto another player, had a clear line of sight, head contact was avoidable and the act was always illegal (tucked
arm, leading with the shoulder). The Player’s actions were highly reckless. By charging into the ruck with a tucked right
shoulder, he knew or should have known that there was a risk of committing the act of foul play.
HCP Step 3: What was the degree of danger?
c. The degree of danger was high. The Committee considered the following factors:
i. Direct contact – the Player’s shoulder made direct contact with USA #4’s head/face;
ii. High force – the Player drives into the USA #4 with force;
ii. Always illegal act -the Player’s right arm is tucked and there is no attempt to bind;
HCP Step 4: Is there any mitigation?
d. The Committee found there was nomitigating factors present.

title: RWC25 FPRC Decision Qawe RSA
text:
FOUL PLAY REVIEW COMMITTEE
DECISION
PARTICULARS OF OFFENCE
Player’s surname Qawe Player’s Chumisa
forename(s)
Player’s Union South Africa
Match South Africa v France (Womens)
Competition RWC25 Match Date 7 September 2025
SELECT: Red card ☒ Citing ☐
Offence Breach of Law 9.13 – A player must not
tackle an opponent early, late or
dangerously. Dangerous tackling includes,
but is not limited to, tackling or attempting
to tackle an opponent above the line of the
shoulders even if the tackle starts below the
line of the shoulders.
Finding of Committee
Foul play determined? Foul Play Determined (plea of guilty)
Red Card Upheld
Red card upheld?
3 matches.
Summary of Sanction
In the event that the Player applies for and successfully completes World Rugby's Coaching
Intervention Programme, the sanction will be reduced by 1 match.
Fixtures to be confirmed.
Matches/tournaments
At a minimum to include Women's World Cup Quarter Final. It will also include the semi-final
included in sanction
should South Africa make it to that fixture (and the final in the event that the World Rugby
Coaching Intervention Program is not applied for and successfully completed by that time).
We are informed that the Player has no other confirmed fixtures beyond the tournament at
this stage. In those circumstances, in the event that South Africa is, for example, knocked out
of the tournament after the Quarter Final, the Player is to notify World Rugby of her playing
schedule as soon as it becomes available so that the FPRC can confirm the fixtures to be
included with the sanction.
REASONS FOR DECISION
• The Player was ordered off following receiving a red card during the fixture.
• The red card was issued for a breach of Law 9.13 – a player must not tackle an opponent early,
late or dangerously. Dangerous tackling includes, but is not limited to, tackling or attempting
to tackle an opponent above the line of the shoulders even if the tackle starts below the line of
the shoulders
• The referee's report is in these terms: "Dangerous tackle, direct contact to head, tackler
upright."
• The FPRO's report is in these terms: "Head contact, foul play, high degree of danger, no
mitigation."
• The video footage identifies an incident consistent with the above description.
Disciplinary Decision Foul Play Review Committee Page 1 of 3

• The medical evidence from France is that "Just spoke with our doctor. Our player is suffering of
an hematoma and bone contusion of the right zygomatic bone subject to clinical and
paraclinical evolution. We will see over the next few days what the outcome is."
The Player submitted that:
• the Player attempted a legitimate wrap tackle but failed to sufficiently lower her body height.
As a result, direct head contact occurred between her and France 11;
• the Player admits foul play, that there was head contact, that the degree of danger was high,
and that the incident warranted a red card;
• the Player's actions were not intentional (but were reckless);
• the Player attempted a legitimate wrap tackle but mistimed her body position;
• no provocation, retaliation or self-defence relevant;
• the victim player continued to play after the incident (and was still awaiting medical report);
• other players did not react as if it were an intentional incident;
• the victim player was not unusually vulnerable; and
• no premeditation.
The FPRC accepts these submissions.
Sanction
The FPRC determined the entry point as being mid-range given World Rugby's directive where there is
a head contact in a breach of 9.13.
The entry point for a mid-range for a dangerous tackle (9.13) is 6 weeks.
Having regard to a plea of guilty (at the first available opportunity), and that the FPRC was informed the
Player apologised to the victim player at the conclusion of the match, and feels remorseful for her
actions (which it accepts), the FPRC is of the view that a 50% reduction is appropriate mitigation in the
circumstances.
The FPRC notes in awarding the full 50% in mitigation that it considered the 2022 red card for a breach
of 9.13. However, there was no sanction imposed in that instance and, having reviewed the decision,
and given the effluxion of time, it believes 50% is the appropriate mitigation in present circumstances.
There were no aggravating circumstances identified by the FPRC.
Accordingly, the sanction proposed to be imposed by the FPRC (if accepted) is a sanction of 3 matches.
The Player has sought (and been granted) leave to apply to World Rugby 's Coaching Intervention
Program. In the event that the Player applies for and successfully completes the Program, the sanction
would be reduced by 1 match.
Disciplinary Decision Foul Play Review Committee Page 2 of 3

At a minimum the Player's sanction will include Women's World Cup Quarter Final. It will also include
the semi-final should South Africa make it to that fixture (and the final in the event that the World
Rugby Coaching Intervention Program is not applied for and successfully completed by that time).
We are informed that the Player has no other confirmed fixtures beyond the tournament at this stage.
In those circumstances, in the event that South Africa is, for example, knocked out of the tournament
after the Quarter Final, the Player is to notify World Rugby of her playing schedule as soon as it becomes
available so that the FPRC can confirm the fixtures to be included with the sanction.
Stephen Hardy (Chair, AU)

Stefan Terblanche (RSA)
Committee Members
Ofisa Tonu'u (NZ)

title: World Rugby FPRC Decision SEU
text:
FOUL PLAY REVIEW COMMITTEE
DECISION
PARTICULARS OF OFFENCE
Player’s surname Seu Player’s Taleni
forename(s)
Player’s Union Samoa
Match Samoa v Fiji
Competition PNC Match Date 6 September 2025
SELECT: Red card ☒ Citing
Offence 2 YC offences: ☐
- Brech of Laws 9.16 and 9.13
Finding of Committee
Foul play determined? Foul Play Determined (two YCs resulting in a RC)
Red Card Upheld
Red card upheld?
1 week
Summary of Sanction
Samoa v USA (14 September 2025)
Matches/tournaments
included in sanction
REASONS FOR DECISION
• The Player was ordered off following receiving 2 yellow cards during the fixture.
First Yellow Card
• The first yellow card, was issued for a breach of Law 9.16 – a player must not charge or knock
down an opponent carrying the ball without attempting to grasp that player.
• A description of the first yellow card is in these terms: "After the ball carrier kicked the ball,
blue 6 late no arms tackle."
• The TMO/FPRO's Report notes "In the 48 min #6 Samoa Taleni Seu tackled #12 Fiji dangerously
by not using his arms in the tackle. The tackle was not considered high danger as there was no
head contact. The tackle started at Yellow card threshold and remained a Yellow card with no
mitigation."
• The video footage identifies an incident consistent with the above.
• The medical evidence is that "#12 was taken off for a precautionary HIA assessment and passed
so that he returned to the game with no issues and post game was symptom free so no
concussion injury was diagnosed."
• The Player provided no evidence or submissions in relation to this incident.
Second Yellow Card (which led to a RC)
• The second yellow card was issued for a breach of Law 9.13 – a player must not tackle an
opponent early, late or dangerously. Dangerous tackling includes, but is not limited to, tackling
or attempting to tackle an opponent above the line of the shoulders even if the tackle starts
below the line of the shoulders
Disciplinary Decision Foul Play Review Committee Page 1 of 2

• A description of the second yellow card incident is in these terms: "After the ball was passed
blue 6 completed a late tackle. This was a second yellow card so red card issued".
• The video footage identifies
• The medical evidence is that "#10 had a hit to the rib cage which didn't cause him to come off
so he finished the game with bruising over his rib cage region. He will be [fit] to play next week."
The Player's submits, in relation to incident 2, that:
"At the time of the incident, I was committed to making a defensive tackle. I already initiated my motion
towards the ball carrier prior to the pass being made. Given the speed and dynamics of rugby, I was
unable to alter my trajectory once the ball was passed, and I immediately adjusted to make the tackle
on the player in question.
The distance between myself and the ball carrier at the moment the pass was thrown contributed to the
perceived severity of the impact. I did not have the ability to pull out of the tackle or reduce the
momentum as I had already committed to the action. The timing of the pass, in conjunction with my
positioning on the field, made the contact appear worse than the intent behind it."
The FPRC found that the tackle was sufficiently late to warrant a yellow card and that the Player needed
to take more care in the execution and timing of the tackle.
Sanction
The FPRC considered an appropriate entry point for the RC (2 YCs) at 2 weeks (reflecting Low End nature
of offending). The FPRC found the offending to be reckless, but not higher than YC in each instance.
The FPRC noted there was no ongoing medical issue on either victim player – with both victim players
having continued the match (other than a HIA assessment in the first incident (which the victim player
passed)).
Having regard to a plea of guilty and the Player's disciplinary record, should the FPRC offer be accepted,
the FPRC determined a 50% reduction was appropriate mitigation in the circumstances.
There were no aggravating circumstances identified by the FPRC.
Accordingly, the sanction proposed to be imposed by the FPRC (if accepted) is a sanction of 1 week,
with the Player to miss Samoa v USA fixture on 14 September 2025.
Stephen Hardy (Chair, AU)
